Meta.title: The Long Watch
Meta.description: 25 years of the planet's fires, harmonised from MODIS and VIIRS and told by the satellites that watched them.

Story.writerFigures: Figures for this chapter's text (use as placeholders in messages/*.json):

c3.title: What 375 metres sees
c3.text: I am Suomi-NPP. I see the ground in <fig>375 m</fig> squares; MODIS sees it in <fig>1 km</fig> squares. A small fire inside one of its pixels is often missed. On the same days, raw MODIS counts <fig>{rawGap}</fig> fewer fires than I do.

c5.title: The year Canada burned
c5.text: I am Terra. I cross Canada every morning at about ten. In <fig>{year}</fig> the country's official fire map recorded <fig>{burned} Mha</fig> burned. That is <fig>{ratio}×</fig> the average season since {firstYear}, and more than {seasons, plural, one {the season} other {the # seasons}} before it combined.

c8.title: The drift
c8.text: My orbit is drifting. I used to pass over at <fig>{terraFrom}</fig> local time; by {lastYear} it was <fig>{terraTo}</fig>. Aqua drifts the other way, from <fig>{aquaFrom}</fig> to <fig>{aquaTo}</fig>. Fires burn hardest in mid-afternoon, so the hour we pass changes what we see.
